summary: Round 3 was applied carefully. Every review-3 finding is fixed as written, check.mjs is clean (ready_to_publish true, must_fix 0, links checked), and the final is now answerable from the options in 6 of 15 questions (target 7 or fewer). One problem remains, and it is must-fix: m08-q4’s key is right, but the question is unfair. M8 card 3 says “Disconnect when the job is done” with no exception, and M8 t2’s model answer says to disconnect “after each weekly run”, which is the option both the cards and blind tests chose. The scenario’s deciding fact (“she is on site every Monday”) is also ambiguous: “on site” can mean “at the office”, and “she” can mean the intern. The fixes are small and exact (one card sentence, one model answer, two scenario sentences, one why_wrong) and can be applied without another review round; once they are in, the programme meets the ready rule.
strengths: Every review-3 rewrite went in as specified, and the clue tests confirm them: f03, f09, f11, m10-q4 and m11-q1 are no longer answered from the options, and the blind test now agrees with m01-q4.

The final is fair to place learners skill by skill: options-only 6 of 15 (down from 11), blind 15 of 15. The six it gets (f04, f08, f10, f12, f14, f15) all need the scenario or rest on a principle that is the skill.

Rule 28 is now met: counting check-ins, the ask-the-AI family is a wrong option in four places (m05-q2, aa-m03-c1, aa-m06-c2, aa-m07-c2) and the right answer in m06-q4. Rule 30 is met: the aa-m01-c3, aa-m03-c1 and aa-m09-c2 hints point to the idea, not the answer.
Accuracy holds: M4 card 2 and m04-q3 now say “May 2027”, which matches every source I found; no notice shortening the DPDP timeline could be found today.

findings.problem: m08-q4 (cards test missed it; blind test disagreed, choosing “Only the calendar, read-only, disconnected after each week’s summary”). Ruling: the key is right, but the question is ambiguous and partly untaught. (1) Untaught and contradicted: M8 card 3 teaches “Disconnect when the job is done” with no exception for a standing approval, and t2’s model answer (“after”) says a weekly summary “disconnects after each weekly run”. A learner who follows the module picks the wrong option, and rule 21 applies: the module recommends the step the question marks wrong. (2) Ambiguous fact: “Reconnecting needs the manager’s admin login, and she is on site every Monday.” “On site” also means “at the workplace”, which makes reconnecting easy and disconnecting right; the blueprint row itself reads it as “away on Mondays”. And “she” can mean the intern, who is the subject of the stem “What should she connect?”.
findings.fix: Scenario: “Arjun, an intern at an architecture studio in Thiruvananthapuram, writes the weekly summary of site visits with AI every Monday. The visits are in the studio’s Google Calendar. The manager has approved read access to the calendar only, for the weekly summary, until the project ends in March. Only she can reconnect it, with her admin login, and she spends every Monday at building sites with no laptop.” Question: “What should Arjun connect?” Keep the four options and the key. Explanation: “Least privilege means only the access the task needs, for as long as it needs it. The approval covers the calendar every week until March, so the calendar stays connected, nothing else is, and it is disconnected when the project ends.” why_wrong, first sentence: “Disconnecting would suit a one-off approval; this one runs to March, and only the manager can reconnect, but she is at building sites every Monday.” Keep the other two why_wrong sentences. Blueprint row: “Decided by: approval runs to March; only the manager can reconnect, and she is at building sites every Monday”.
findings.source: Clue tests (cards and blind, run 4), agentic-ai.probes.json

findings.problem: M8 doesn’t teach what m08-q4 tests, and its t2 model answer teaches the opposite. Card 3 says only “Disconnect when the job is done”, so “for as long as it needs” (the explanation’s reason) appears nowhere in the cards; t2’s “after” says the plan “disconnects after each weekly run, or at the end of the internship”.
findings.fix: Card 3: replace “Disconnect when the job is done.” with “Disconnect when the job is done: after a one-off task, or when the approval for a repeating task ends.” (card goes from 135 to about 149 words). t2 “after”: replace “It disconnects after each weekly run, or at the end of the internship.” with “It stays connected only while the manager’s approval runs, and is disconnected when that approval or the internship ends.” Workbook term “Least privilege”: “Giving only the access a task needs, for only as long as it needs it.”

findings.problem: Ruling on options-only 58% (34 of 59; 88%, 73%, 61% in earlier runs). It is acceptable now. The final, which places learners, is at 6 of 15, within target. The 28 quiz questions it got are the module’s core principle applied to a case that confirms it (as ruled in review 3), and the nine it was certain of are fair: m02-q2 (say the office will confirm what the facts don’t cover) and m02-q3 (a fresh brief in a new chat) are M2’s two headline habits; m05-q2 and m05-q4 are M5’s stakes-and-checkability rule and the tutor prompt; m07-q1 and m07-q2 are primary source and “Not confirmed”; m11-q3 turns on three stated constraints (phone, no budget, approval); f08 is the official current source; f14 is discussed below. Pushing further would mean making foundation principles unguessable, which tests trickery, not skill. Rule 32 is met in every quiz and the final (6 flips). Re-test only after learners answer: if any of these shows over 90% first-time correct with 30+ answers, rewrite it as a flip.
findings.fix: No change now. After launch, run scorecard.mjs on Question health data and rewrite any question here that 30+ learners answer at over 90%.

findings.problem: f14 keys the careful value in both parts (check all three statistics; add a note), which rule 34 forbids, and the options test was certain of it. I accept it: the case genuinely needs both (the college rule requires the note; the conclusion rests on all three), the final is within target, and the blind test agrees. Flipping a part would need a fact that makes one careful step merely unnecessary, which rule 21 says is not wrong.
findings.fix: Keep f14. If Question health later shows it over 90% first-time correct, replace it with a case where one part’s quick value is right (for example, the teammate’s appendix already discloses the AI use, so Neha’s job is only the statistics).

lessons.rule: Before keying a flip (a right answer that bends a module habit, such as staying connected or skipping a re-check), search that module’s Learn cards, task hints, task model answers (“after”) and check-ins for the habit stated without exception. Add the condition under which it bends to the card, and rewrite any model answer that gives the opposite advice.
lessons.why: In Agentic AI round 3, m08-q4 keyed “left connected” while M8 card 3 said “Disconnect when the job is done” and t2’s model answer said “disconnects after each weekly run”; both the cards test and the blind test chose the habit.

lessons.rule: When a scenario has two people, name the one the stem asks about, and write the deciding fact so it can’t point to the other person (a name, not “she”). Avoid words with an everyday second meaning in the deciding fact (“on site”, “off”, “out”): say plainly where the person is and what they can’t do.
lessons.why: m08-q4’s deciding fact was “she is on site every Monday”: “she” could be the intern in the stem, and “on site” can mean “at the office”, which made the wrong option right.
